title: Introduction to Number Systems
content: A number system is a way of representing and classifying numbers. In Algebra, the most common number systems are natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers, and irrational numbers.
example: The number 5 is a natural number, whole number, integer, rational number, and real number.

title: Natural and Whole Numbers
content: Natural numbers are commonly used for counting. They are 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on. Whole numbers include all natural numbers together with zero.
example: 7 is both a natural number and a whole number. 0 is a whole number but is not included in the natural numbers under this definition.

title: Integers
content: Integers include positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero. They do not contain fractional or decimal parts.
example: -8, 0, and 15 are integers, while 2.5 is not an integer.

title: Rational and Irrational Numbers
content: A rational number can be written as a ratio of two integers where the denominator is not zero. Irrational numbers cannot be written as a ratio of two integers and have non-terminating, non-repeating decimal representations.
formula: Rational: a/b, where a,b ∈ Z and b ≠ 0
example: 3/4 is rational because it is a ratio of two integers. √2 is irrational because its decimal representation is non-terminating and non-repeating.

title: Real Numbers
content: Real numbers consist of both rational and irrational numbers. Every point on the number line represents a real number.
formula: Real Numbers = Rational Numbers ∪ Irrational Numbers
